assumptions: The matrix dimension m and the number r of Householder applications are positive.
The exact transformations are P_j=I-v_j v_j^T with v_j^T v_j=2; their involutory identity P_j^2=I is carried as the derived algebraic certificate used to factor Q^T.
The computed vector is the sequential perturbed product (P_r+DeltaP_r)...(P_1+DeltaP_1)b, and its value at model.unitRoundoff is linked to a Model 1.5 scalar-operation trace.
With probability one, every local DeltaP_j satisfies the subordinate matrix 2-norm bound (4.2).
On that same event, the unit-roundoff-indexed local family satisfies DeltaP_j(u)=O(u), which is the asymptotic content needed to type the matrix O(u^2) term in (4.8).
The standard relative-error model is used; the source states no separate overflow, underflow, NaN, or infinity clauses for Lemma 4.2.

formal_statement.plain_language: A computed sequence of normalized Householder applications equals its exact result plus all single local-perturbation insertions and a matrix O(u^2) remainder; equivalently the error factors through Q^T and the exact F_j matrices of equation (4.9).

informal_proof: Induct on the number of applications to split the perturbed product into zero-, one-, and multiple-DeltaP terms. Closure of entrywise big-O under finite matrix sums and products gives O(u^2) for the multiple-perturbation matrix on the probability-one local event. Use P_j^2=I to show the one-insertion matrix equals Q^T times the sum of F_j, then absorb the higher-order matrix through the same orthogonal factor.
informal_statement: Both displayed first-order expansions in equation (4.8), including the exact endpoint ordering in equation (4.9), for the Model 1.5 computed Householder application.
